text: Growth as the job is to connect users to the value of your product. Growth sometimes gets this reputation that it's just pure metrics hacking.
speaker: Albert Cheng
context: Lenny asks Albert about his definition of growth and how to approach growth work effectively. Albert explains his core philosophy about what growth teams should focus on, contrasting it with common misconceptions about growth being purely about manipulating metrics without regard for user value.
text_ko: 성장은 사용자와 제품의 가치를 연결하는 일이에요. 가끔 성장이라는 개념이 단순히 수치 조작으로만 여겨지기도 해요.
text_zh: 增长的任务是将用户与产品的价值连接起来。有时，增长会被认为只是单纯的指标黑客（metrics hacking）。
text_es: El crecimiento consiste en conectar a los usuarios con el valor de tu producto. A veces, el crecimiento adquiere la reputación de ser solo un juego de métricas.
key_sentence: Growth connects users to product value, not just pure metrics hacking.

vocabulary.definition: To join or link together; to establish a relationship or communication between entities.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'connect' often refers to the process of linking customers with products or services that meet their needs, thereby enhancing user engagement and satisfaction.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'connect' can imply a simple link, in a business context it often carries the connotation of creating meaningful relationships that foster loyalty and trust.

vocabulary.definition: The importance, worth, or usefulness of something; a principle or standard of behavior that is considered important in a particular context.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, 'value' refers to the benefits that a product or service provides to customers, which can drive purchasing decisions and brand loyalty.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'value' can also imply a subjective assessment, varying from one customer to another based on their individual needs and preferences.

vocabulary.definition: Quantitative measures used to assess, compare, and track performance or production.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business and tech sectors, 'metrics' are critical for evaluating the effectiveness of strategies, products, and marketing campaigns, often guiding decision-making processes.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'metrics' can provide valuable insights, an overemphasis on quantitative data may overlook qualitative factors that are equally important for understanding user experience.

text: User retention is gold for consumer subscription companies. If you don't retain your users, then a lot of the onus is on getting them to pay on day one.
speaker: Albert Cheng
context: Lenny asks Albert what he thinks is the biggest missing piece that people don't understand about building successful consumer subscription products. Albert emphasizes that retention is the most critical factor, explaining that without good retention, companies are forced into the much harder task of converting users immediately upon signup rather than building long-term value.
text_ko: 사용자 유지가 소비자 구독 회사에겐 정말 중요해요. 만약 사용자를 잘 유지하지 못하면, 첫날에 결제하게 만드는 게 정말 큰 부담이 되거든요.
text_zh: 用户留存对消费订阅公司来说至关重要。如果无法留住用户，那么在第一天就让他们付费的压力就会很大。
text_es: La retención de usuarios es clave para las empresas de suscripción. Si no logras retener a tus usuarios, gran parte de la responsabilidad recae en conseguir que paguen desde el primer día.
key_sentence: User retention is gold; the onus is on retaining users, not just initial payment.

vocabulary.definition: User retention refers to the ability of a company to keep its customers engaged and using its products or services over a period of time.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of subscription-based businesses, high user retention is crucial as it directly impacts revenue stability and growth, reducing the need for constant customer acquisition.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often implies a focus on long-term engagement rather than just initial sales, highlighting the importance of customer satisfaction and loyalty.

vocabulary.definition: Onus refers to a burden or responsibility that is placed on someone to fulfill a duty or obligation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, the term is often used to indicate accountability, such as the onus being on a company to ensure customer satisfaction or compliance with regulations.
vocabulary.nuance: Using 'onus' can imply a heavier or more serious responsibility, often suggesting that failure to meet this obligation could lead to negative consequences.

vocabulary.definition: Subscription companies are businesses that offer products or services to customers on a recurring basis, typically charging a fee at regular intervals.
vocabulary.businessContext: These companies rely on a steady stream of revenue from subscribers, making user retention and customer satisfaction critical to their business model.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often connotes a modern, tech-savvy approach to business, appealing to consumers who prefer convenience and ongoing access over one-time purchases.

text: The lived product experience for most of the free users was that Grammarly was just a product to fix your spelling and grammar because those were the free suggestions.
speaker: Albert Cheng
context: Lenny asks Albert about his biggest monetization win at Grammarly, based on a recommendation from Noam Levinsky. Albert explains how they discovered that free users only saw basic spelling and grammar corrections, giving them a limited view of Grammarly's capabilities. By mixing in samples of premium features with the free suggestions, they completely changed how users perceived the product's value.
text_ko: 대부분의 무료 사용자들(free users)이 실제로 체감한 제품 경험(lived product experience)은 Grammarly가 맞춤법과 문법만 고쳐주는 제품이라는 거였어요. 그 이유는 무료로 제공되는 제안(suggestions)이 바로 그 기능들이었기 때문이에요.
text_zh: 对于大部分免费用户来说，他们实际体验到的就是Grammarly只是个改错别字和语法的工具，因为免费版本就只提供这些建议。
text_es: Para la mayoría de usuarios gratuitos, su experiencia real con el producto era que Grammarly solo servía para corregir ortografía y gramática, porque esas eran las únicas sugerencias que venían gratis.
key_sentence: The lived product experience for free users limits their perception of Grammarly's power.
original_text: The lived product experience for most of the free users was that Grammarly was just a product to fix your spelling and grammar because those were the free suggestions. What if we actually sampled a number of different paid suggestions and interspersed them to free users across their writing? All of a sudden, people were seeing Grammarly as a much more powerful tool than they were before.

vocabulary.definition: Proposals or recommendations put forward for consideration or action.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, suggestions often refer to user feedback or enhancements that can improve a product's functionality or user experience.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can imply a level of informality, and while suggestions are valuable, they may not always be prioritized in decision-making processes.

vocabulary.definition: The process of personally encountering or undergoing something, often leading to knowledge or skill acquisition.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, particularly in tech, user experience (UX) is a critical focus area, as it directly impacts customer satisfaction and retention.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can encompass both positive and negative encounters, so it's important to specify the type of experience when discussing user interactions.

text: I saw some of the highest performers just being people that had very high agency, had that clock speed, had that energy, but they didn't necessarily need to have deep experience on that matter.
speaker: Albert Cheng
context: Lenny asks Albert about the most counterintuitive lesson he's learned about building teams. Albert shares his observation that the best team members aren't always those with the most experience in a specific domain. Instead, he's found that people with high agency, quick decision-making speed, and energy often outperform more experienced candidates, particularly in rapidly changing environments where past knowledge may become obsolete.
text_ko: 제가 본 최고 성과자들 중 일부는 주도성(agency)이 아주 높고, 속도감(clock speed)이 빠르며, 에너지가 넘쳤어요. 그런데 꼭 그 일에 대한 깊은 경험이 필요한 건 아니었어요.
text_zh: 我发现那些表现最出色的人，就是那些执行力特别强、反应特别快、精力特别充沛的人，但他们不一定非要在这个领域有多深的经验。
text_es: Vi que algunos de los mejores talentos eran simplemente personas con mucha iniciativa propia (high agency), que se movían rápido, que tenían esa energía, pero no necesariamente tenían que ser expertos en el tema.
key_sentence: the highest performers just being people that had very high agency, had that clock speed, had that energy
original_text: I saw some of the highest performers just being people that had very high agency, had that clock speed, had that energy, but they didn't necessarily need to have deep experience on that matter. Sometimes experience could be a crutch, especially in this world where the grounds are shifting so fast with AI. A lot of your learned habits actually need to be intentionally discarded.

vocabulary.definition: High agency refers to an individual's ability to take initiative and make choices that significantly influence their circumstances and outcomes.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, high agency is valued as it indicates a proactive mindset, enabling employees to drive projects forward and adapt to challenges effectively.
vocabulary.nuance: While high agency is often seen as a positive trait, it can be perceived negatively if it leads to overstepping boundaries or disregarding team dynamics.

vocabulary.definition: Clock speed refers to the pace at which an organization or individual can process information, make decisions, and execute actions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In fast-paced business environments, a high clock speed is crucial for maintaining competitive advantage and responding swiftly to market changes.
vocabulary.nuance: While a high clock speed is generally advantageous, it can lead to rushed decisions if not balanced with thorough analysis.

vocabulary.definition: Deep experience refers to extensive knowledge and expertise gained through prolonged involvement in a specific field or subject matter.
vocabulary.businessContext: In many industries, deep experience is highly valued as it contributes to informed decision-making and mentorship within teams.
vocabulary.nuance: While deep experience is beneficial, it may also lead to rigidity in thinking; thus, it should be complemented with openness to new ideas.

text: When you're in exploratory mode, think of it as finding the right mountain to climb. And then when you're in exploitation mode, it's like focusing your resources on climbing that mountain effectively.
speaker: Albert Cheng
context: Lenny asks Albert to explain his 'explore and exploit' framework for finding growth opportunities. Albert describes this as a balance between two modes: exploration (finding new opportunities and testing different approaches) and exploitation (doubling down on what works). He warns that companies often get stuck focusing too heavily on one mode, either scattering their efforts across too many experiments or getting trapped in local optimization.
text_ko: 탐색 모드(exploratory mode)일 땐 어떤 산을 오를지 찾는 과정이라고 생각하세요. 그다음 활용 모드(exploitation mode)일 땐 그 산을 효과적으로 오르기 위해 자원을 집중하는 거예요.
text_zh: 当你处于探索阶段的时候，就像是在找对的山头去爬。然后当你进入深耕阶段，就是要集中资源，把这座山爬好爬到位。
text_es: Cuando estás en modo exploración, piénsalo como encontrar la montaña correcta para escalar. Y después, cuando pasas al modo de explotación, es como enfocar todos tus recursos en subir esa montaña de la manera más eficiente.
key_sentence: think of it as finding the right mountain to climb.
original_text: When you're in exploratory mode, think of it as finding the right mountain to climb. And then when you're in exploitation mode, it's like focusing your resources on climbing that mountain effectively. And certain companies, I think the warning is to basically spend too much of your time on one end of the spectrum.

vocabulary.definition: Pertaining to the act of investigating or examining something in order to gain information or insights.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, exploratory phases often involve research and development activities aimed at identifying new opportunities or innovative solutions.
vocabulary.nuance: This term carries a connotation of openness to new ideas and a willingness to take risks, making it suitable for brainstorming sessions or initial project phases.

vocabulary.definition: The act of utilizing resources or opportunities to their fullest potential, often for profit or advantage.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, exploitation refers to the strategic use of assets, capabilities, or market opportunities to maximize returns and achieve competitive advantage.
vocabulary.nuance: While it can imply effective resource use, exploitation may also carry negative connotations related to overuse or unethical practices, so context is crucial.

vocabulary.definition: Assets, materials, or inputs that can be utilized to achieve goals or objectives, including financial, human, and technological resources.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and startups, resources are critical for operations, project development, and strategic planning, influencing overall performance and sustainability.
vocabulary.nuance: The term encompasses both tangible and intangible assets, and its use can imply a focus on efficiency and optimization in resource management.

vocabulary.definition: In a manner that produces the desired result or outcome; efficiently and successfully.
vocabulary.businessContext: Effectiveness is a key performance indicator in business, often used to assess how well strategies, processes, or teams achieve their objectives.
vocabulary.nuance: This term emphasizes not just doing things right, but doing the right things to achieve optimal outcomes, making it essential in performance evaluations.

text: You can just plug in like an analysis that another person wrote and just have it summarized for you and give you advice on ideas to go try. And so that ideation, that research cycle was much, much faster.
speaker: Albert Cheng
context: Lenny asks Albert how AI is changing the work of growth professionals. Albert explains how AI tools like ChatGPT are accelerating the experiment analysis and ideation process. Previously, teams had to manually write analysis documents and extract insights from experiment results, but now AI can quickly summarize findings and suggest new ideas to test, significantly speeding up the cycle from experiment completion to next hypothesis.
text_ko: 다른 사람이 쓴 분석을 그냥 연결해서 요약해주고, 시도해볼 아이디어에 대한 조언도 받을 수 있어요. 그래서 아이디어 구상(ideation)이나 연구 사이클이 훨씬 더 빨라졌죠.
text_zh: 你可以直接输入其他人撰写的分析，然后让它为你总结并提供建议，告诉你可以尝试的想法。因此，这个创意生成（ideation）和研究周期变得快得多。
text_es: Puedes simplemente introducir un análisis que otra persona escribió y obtener un resumen, además de recibir recomendaciones sobre ideas que puedes probar. De esta manera, el proceso de ideación y la investigación se volvieron mucho más rápidos.
key_sentence: Plug in analysis for faster ideation and research cycles.

vocabulary.definition: The process of generating and developing new ideas, often through brainstorming or creative thinking techniques.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and startup environments, ideation is crucial for innovation, product development, and problem-solving, enabling teams to explore diverse solutions.
vocabulary.nuance: While ideation emphasizes creativity, it should be distinguished from mere brainstorming, which may lack structure or focus.

vocabulary.definition: The detailed examination and evaluation of data or information to understand its components and derive insights.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, analysis is essential for decision-making, strategy formulation, and performance assessment, often utilizing various analytical tools and methodologies.
vocabulary.nuance: Analysis can imply a rigorous, systematic approach, but it may also suggest a level of complexity that requires specialized knowledge.

vocabulary.definition: A systematic sequence of steps in conducting research, typically involving planning, data collection, analysis, and dissemination of findings.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, the research cycle is vital for developing evidence-based strategies, understanding market trends, and validating product concepts.
vocabulary.nuance: The research cycle emphasizes iterative learning and refinement, highlighting the importance of feedback and adaptation in research processes.

text: Growth sometimes gets this reputation that it's just pure metrics hacking, like we're cold people that just are trying to move a particular metric up.
speaker: Albert Cheng
context: Lenny asks Albert to elaborate on his definition of growth as 'connecting users to the value of your product.' Albert addresses common negative perceptions of growth teams, explaining that many people view growth professionals as solely focused on manipulating metrics without caring about user experience. He contrasts this with his philosophy of thinking about users holistically and focusing on delivering genuine value.
text_ko: 그로스(growth)는 가끔 '그냥 메트릭 해킹(metrics hacking)만 하는 것'이라는 평판이 있어요. 마치 우리가 차갑게 특정 메트릭(metric)만 올리려 한다는 식으로요.
text_zh: 增长有时候会被误解，好像我们就是纯粹的数据黑客(metrics hacking)，像冷血动物一样只知道把某个指标往上推。
text_es: El crecimiento a veces tiene esta fama de que solo es hackear métricas, como si fuéramos gente fría que simplemente está tratando de subir cierta métrica.
key_sentence: Growth sometimes gets this reputation that it's just pure metrics hacking.
original_text: Growth sometimes gets this reputation that it's just pure metrics hacking, like we're cold people that just are trying to move a particular metric up and we're going to do whatever it can to throw walls and pay walls and add friction in all these spots.

vocabulary.definition: Metrics are quantitative measures used to assess and track performance, progress, or success in various domains.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, metrics are essential for evaluating the effectiveness of strategies, products, and services, often guiding decision-making processes.
vocabulary.nuance: While metrics provide valuable insights, an overemphasis on them can lead to a narrow focus that neglects qualitative factors.

vocabulary.definition: Reputation refers to the beliefs or opinions that are generally held about someone or something, particularly regarding their character or quality.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, reputation is crucial as it can influence customer trust, brand loyalty, and overall market position.
vocabulary.nuance: Reputation is often built over time and can be fragile; it can be positively or negatively impacted by public perception and media coverage.
